summary: All 9 occurrences checked. Stem I has hurting body parts as subjects, with the sufferer expressed by possession: teeth, legs and eyes. Stem III at 62/325 instead has an external pain-causer and a fronted feminine body-part patient apparently resumed by -o-.

naqiri in Hors 1/10 extends the Preterit Intransitive paradigm to plural teeth; it is not the transitive pecking/carving homonym nqr 1. The source's ʕaršan differs from the German first-person singular rendering and is preserved.

Lahdo The snake/7 contrasts onset kәbdela bu nqoro with ensuing knuqro. The same hurting meaning remains in the Infinitiv event and finite predicate; no separate 'throb' sense is needed beyond the existing Ilyas p.c. tooth example.
Hors 1/47 and /48 repeat the existing EL 47/48 material. 66/1, 70/200 and 62/325 are already quoted. Reject duplicate thin-cell additions rather than inflate counts.

Jan 1.21/1017 Manqarle lebi follows a rifle-butt blow to the shoulder. This supports inherited III heftige Schmerzen bereiten with a possessed body-part patient; the human experiencer is available through -i in lebi and the preceding first-person context.

The L-series -le indexes a masculine actor/causer. The verse does not settle whether the understood causer of Manqarle is the gendarme, the blow or its instrument; the machine English It does not settle this.
The shoulder-to-heart pain may be felt bodily or described with expressive force. No separate emotional-hurt sense is established from lebi alone.
